source_text: IV. Galerius Maximus collocutus cum concilio sententiam vix et aegre dixit verbis huiusmodi: Diu sacrilega mente vixisti et plurimos nefariae tibi conspirationis homines adgregasti et inimicum te diis Romanis et sacris legibus constituisti, nec te pii et sacratissimi principes Valerianus et Gallienus Augusti et Valerianus nobilissimus Caesar ad sectam caeremoniarum suarum revocare potuerunt. et ideo cum sis nequissimorum criminum auctor et signifer deprehensus, eris ipse documento his quos scelere tuo tecum adgregasti: sanguine tuo sancietur disciplina. et his dictis decretum ex tabella recitavit: Thascium Cyprianum gladio animadverti placet. Cyprianus episcopus dixit: Deo gratias.
thought_title: The sentence of death by the sword
orientation: Galerius Maximus, the governor who retries Cyprian after exile, speaks the sentence after conferring with his council.
pass_a_gloss: Galerius Maximus, having conferred with the council, spoke the sentence with difficulty and unwillingly in words of this kind: You have lived for a long time with sacrilegious mind and you have gathered to yourself very many men of a wicked conspiracy and you have made yourself an enemy to the Roman gods and to the sacred laws, nor were the dutiful and most sacred emperors Valerian and Gallienus Augusti and Valerian most noble Caesar able to recall you to the sect of their worship rites. And therefore, since you have been caught as author and bearer of the standard of most worthless crimes, you yourself will be for a warning to those whom you have gathered with you by your crime: by your blood discipline will be made binding. And with these things said he recited the decree from the tablet: It is decided that Thascius Cyprian be punished by the sword. Cyprian the bishop said: Thanks to God.

choices.english: to the sect of their worship rites
choices.why: keeps brief glossary worship rites for caeremoniarum and keeps sectam literal rather than smoothing to practice

choices.english: author and bearer of the standard
choices.why: preserves two distinct legal and military images instead of merging them
dative of purpose means a public example to deter others, not a written paper

choices.english: it is decided that Thascius Cyprian be punished by the sword
choices.why: placet is formal council decision language and animadverti with ablative is the penal formula
rejected: he shall die by the sword

pass_b_english: After conferring with his council, Galerius Maximus pronounced the sentence, only with difficulty and reluctance, in these words: "You have lived for a long time with a sacrilegious mind. You have gathered very many followers of a wicked conspiracy to yourself. You have made yourself an enemy to the Roman gods and the sacred laws. Even the dutiful and most sacred rulers Valerian and Gallienus, the emperors, and Valerian, the most noble Caesar, could not bring you back to the sect of their worship rites."

"Therefore, since you have been caught as the author and bearer of the standard of the vilest crimes, you yourself will serve as a warning to those you gathered with you through your crime. Discipline will be made binding by your blood." After saying this, he read the decree from the tablet: "It is decided that Thascius Cyprian be punished by the sword." Cyprian the bishop said, "Thanks be to God."
